purpose: Repair assurance, compatibility and accounting gaps without rerunning valid A or C campaigns.
model: Fixed-feasibility binary knapsack, positive integer weights, capacity, signed integer affine profits, rational t.
inputs: Reuse C heldout-n18-0, heldout-factor and crossing. Use C heldout-n20-2 only for memory stress if needed. No new mathematical samples and no inferred recovery of B models.
order: Rotate paired/three-way method order by repetition; report all raw trials and medians without significance claims.

setup.packages: Debian trixie MPFR/Boost development prerequisites via signed archive metadata; local extraction outside Git
setup.verification: Preserve APT signature/hash and TLS verification. Source Git commit identities, binary hashes, commands and failed attempts recorded.

completion_setup_amendment.reason: Development SCIP certificate on heldout-factor contains lin weak derivations even with separation disabled. Official viprcomp is required. CMake 4.4 rejects upstream TBB's old minimum; use supported CMake 3.31.6 without editing upstream sources.

R111_112: If exact build works, use actual SCIP certificate logging without presolve transformations, complete with official viprcomp when required, independently check and weaken final bounds. No substitute success status if unavailable.
R113: Unchanged frozen VIPR source compiled into a disclosed wrapper. Persistent pristine parent forks a clean child per proof, avoids repeated exec/loader startup; children never modify parent verifier state. Compare direct checker per request on identical valid-A/false-A/valid-B/malformed/valid-A order. Include child CPU, fork/IPC/startup and state controls.
R114: Original-problem native producer -> encoding/VIPR compiler -> proof write -> external checker -> model/primal/hash admission -> lookup/output. Disjoint CPU phases plus entire total and residual. Child user/system CPU included; imports/install/audit separate.
R_admission: Produce and externally admit identical endpoint facts for a fixed model. Replay endpoint checks at every observation versus one immutable admission per run. New queries may reuse only equal-packing optimal endpoints and the inherited fixed-affine endpoint implication; failure probes and checked-point fallback charged.
R_scip: Ordinary cold SCIP vs objective reoptimization on same integer streams, each followed by the same complete external native/VIPR certification. Solver status does not serve as a certificate. Exact SCIP reoptimization explicitly unsupported if source/API declares it unimplemented.
R119: Use actual point and immutable snapshot caches. Trace retained Python cache allocations and serialized proof bytes separately. Sample simultaneous RSS of runner and all descendants while checking; report sample interval, observed aggregate peak and sampling limitations, never sum separate lifetime maxima.
R120: Cache keys include canonical model and an explicit dependency epoch. Change capacity, weight, rational objective, domain, nonlinear term, and dependency epoch on live cache. Evict/reject old facts; recertify only supported affine binary models. Restoring a prior model does not resurrect entries evicted by an epoch update. External proof file edits do not invalidate already immutable admitted facts unless explicit refresh is requested.
acceptance: Independent exact subset oracle validates all answers and endpoint obligations; unchanged VIPR checker replays every distinct new proof and all false-bound controls; cache event traces checked independently; every requested unsupported feature remains a named status. Replication uses fresh directories and identical source/input/dependency hashes, compares mathematical outputs and underlying proof hashes separately from named timing/RSS/path fields.
novelty: Credit classical endpoint interpolation, scaling, caching, DP, reoptimization and established proof checking. The fork wrapper and accounting are experimental engineering; no literature priority inferred. Empirical differences scoped to these reused fixtures.
